# Meemaw

> Meemaw is an elegant, lightweight React utility component library that eliminates repetitive JSX patterns. Zero dependencies, <10KB, tree-shakeable, TypeScript-first, SSR compatible. Install with `npm install meemaw`. Requires React >=16.8.0.

## Overview

Meemaw provides 9 declarative React components for conditional rendering, iteration, time-based display, and user interaction. All components are imported from the `meemaw` package. The library has zero dependencies beyond React as a peer dependency, ships full TypeScript declarations, and supports both CommonJS and ESM.

Package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/meemaw
Repository: https://github.com/spiderocious/meemaw
License: MIT
Version: 1.0.2
Bundle size: ~7KB minified + gzipped

## Installation

```bash
npm install meemaw
# or: yarn add meemaw
# or: pnpm add meemaw
```

Peer dependencies: react >=16.8.0, react-dom >=16.8.0

## Exports

```typescript
// Components
export { Switch, Case, Default } from 'meemaw'
export { Show } from 'meemaw'
export { Hidden, BREAKPOINTS } from 'meemaw'
export { Loadable } from 'meemaw'
export { Repeat } from 'meemaw'
export { Delayed } from 'meemaw'
export { ShowOnce } from 'meemaw'
export { CopyToClipboard } from 'meemaw'
export { Clamp } from 'meemaw'

// Types
export type { Breakpoint, HiddenProps } from 'meemaw'
export type { LoadableProps } from 'meemaw'
export type { DelayedProps } from 'meemaw'
export type { ShowOnceProps, PersistenceType } from 'meemaw'
export type { CopyToClipboardProps } from 'meemaw'
export type { ClampProps } from 'meemaw'
```

## Components

### Switch, Case, Default

Match-case pattern for multiple conditions. Renders the first matching `Case`. If none match, renders `Default`. Returns null if no match and no Default.

Props:
- `Switch`: children: ReactNode
- `Case`: when: boolean, children: ReactNode
- `Default`: children: ReactNode

```tsx
import { Switch, Case, Default } from 'meemaw';

<Switch>
  <Case when={status === 'pending'}>Processing...</Case>
  <Case when={status === 'shipped'}>On the way!</Case>
  <Case when={status === 'delivered'}>Delivered</Case>
  <Default>Unknown status</Default>
</Switch>
```

Behavior: Only the first matching Case renders. Order matters. If multiple Defaults exist, the last one wins.

### Show

Conditional rendering with optional fallback. Replaces ternary operators in JSX.

Props:
- when?: boolean — primary condition
- if?: boolean — alias for `when` (`when` takes precedence if both provided)
- fallback?: ReactNode — shown when condition is false (default: null)
- children: ReactNode — shown when condition is true

```tsx
import { Show } from 'meemaw';

<Show when={isLoggedIn} fallback={<Login />}>
  <Dashboard />
</Show>

<Show if={hasPermission} fallback={<AccessDenied />}>
  <AdminPanel />
</Show>
```

### Hidden

Hide content conditionally or by responsive breakpoint. Removes content from the DOM (returns null) when hidden.

Props:
- when?: boolean — hide when true
- if?: boolean — alias for `when`
- on?: Breakpoint | Breakpoint[] — responsive breakpoint(s) to hide on
- children: ReactNode

Breakpoint type: 'mobile' | 'tablet' | 'desktop'

Built-in breakpoints (exported as BREAKPOINTS constant):
- mobile: viewport < 768px
- tablet: viewport < 1024px
- desktop: viewport >= 1024px

`when` and `on` are combined with OR logic. Listens to window resize events. SSR safe (defaults to 'desktop').

```tsx
import { Hidden } from 'meemaw';

<Hidden when={!isPublic}>
  <SecretContent />
</Hidden>

<Hidden on="mobile">
  <DesktopNav />
</Hidden>

<Hidden on={['mobile', 'tablet']}>
  <DesktopOnlyFeature />
</Hidden>
```

### Loadable

Handle async operation states (loading, error, success) with built-in default UI.

Props:
- loading?: boolean — show loading state (default: false)
- error?: boolean | Error | string — show error state (default: false)
- loadingComponent?: ReactNode — custom loading UI (default: animated spinner)
- errorComponent?: ReactNode | ((error: Error | string) => ReactNode) — custom error UI (default: red error box)
- children: ReactNode — success content

Priority: loading > error > children. If loading is true, error and children are ignored.

Default spinner: 20x20px animated circular spinner (CSS keyframes, 0.6s rotation).
Default error: red box (#fee background, #c00 text) displaying "Error: {message}".

```tsx
import { Loadable } from 'meemaw';

<Loadable loading={loading} error={error}>
  <UserProfile data={data} />
</Loadable>

<Loadable
  loading={isLoading}
  error={error}
  loadingComponent={<CustomSpinner />}
  errorComponent={(err) => <div>Failed: {String(err)}</div>}
>
  <Content />
</Loadable>
```

### Repeat

Iterate over arrays or repeat elements n times.

Props (generic: Repeat<T>):
- times?: number — repeat n times (0-based index)
- each?: T[] — array to iterate (takes priority over `times`)
- children: ((item: T, index: number) => ReactNode) | ReactNode

If children is a function, it receives (item, index). If static, it is cloned for each iteration.

```tsx
import { Repeat } from 'meemaw';

// Repeat n times
<Repeat times={5}>
  {(_, index) => <Star key={index} />}
</Repeat>

// Iterate array
<Repeat each={users}>
  {(user, index) => <UserCard key={user.id} user={user} />}
</Repeat>

// Static children repeated
<Repeat times={3}>
  <Divider />
</Repeat>
```

TypeScript: supports generic type inference via `<Repeat<User> each={users}>`.

### Delayed

Delay rendering until a condition is met or a timeout expires.

Props:
- until?: boolean — show when this becomes true (ignores `till`)
- till?: Date | number — show after delay (number = milliseconds, Date = absolute time)
- fallback?: ReactNode — shown while waiting (default: null)
- children: ReactNode

If `until` is provided, `till` is ignored. If `till` is <= 0, content shows immediately. Cleans up timer on unmount.

```tsx
import { Delayed } from 'meemaw';

<Delayed till={3000}>
  <Announcement />
</Delayed>

<Delayed till={new Date('2025-01-01')}>
  <NewYearMessage />
</Delayed>

<Delayed until={dataLoaded} fallback={<Loading />}>
  <DataView />
</Delayed>
```

### ShowOnce

Display content only once, with optional persistence across sessions.

Props:
- for?: number — duration in ms to show before hiding (optional)
- persist?: boolean — enable persistence (default: false)
- persistKey?: string — custom storage key (auto-generated if omitted)
- persistType?: PersistenceType — storage type (default: 'local')
- children: ReactNode

PersistenceType: 'local' | 'session' | 'memory'
- 'local': localStorage — survives reload and browser close
- 'session': sessionStorage — survives reload, cleared when tab closes
- 'memory': in-memory Map — cleared on page reload

Storage key prefix: `meemaw_showonce_`. SSR safe (checks typeof window).

```tsx
import { ShowOnce } from 'meemaw';

<ShowOnce for={5000} persist>
  <WelcomeBanner />
</ShowOnce>

<ShowOnce persist persistType="session">
  <NewFeatureTooltip />
</ShowOnce>

<ShowOnce persist persistKey="onboarding-v1" persistType="local">
  <OnboardingTour />
</ShowOnce>

<ShowOnce persist persistType="memory">
  <FirstTimeHint />
</ShowOnce>
```

### CopyToClipboard

Copy text to clipboard with success/error handling and render function pattern.

Props:
- text?: string — text to copy (if omitted, extracted from children's text content)
- onSuccess?: () => void — callback on successful copy
- onError?: (error: Error) => void — callback on failed copy
- children: ReactNode | ((copy: () => void, copied: boolean) => ReactNode)

If children is a function, it receives (copy, copied) for manual control. If children is a React element, onClick is automatically added. The `copied` state resets to false after 2000ms.

Uses navigator.clipboard.writeText() with a fallback to document.execCommand('copy') for legacy browsers.

```tsx
import { CopyToClipboard } from 'meemaw';

<CopyToClipboard text="npm install meemaw">
  <button>Copy command</button>
</CopyToClipboard>

<CopyToClipboard text={shareUrl}>
  {(copy, copied) => (
    <button onClick={copy}>
      {copied ? 'Copied!' : 'Copy link'}
    </button>
  )}
</CopyToClipboard>

<CopyToClipboard
  text={code}
  onSuccess={() => toast.success('Copied!')}
  onError={(err) => toast.error(err.message)}
>
  <CopyButton />
</CopyToClipboard>

// Auto-extract text from children
<CopyToClipboard>
  <code>const x = 42;</code>
</CopyToClipboard>
```

### Clamp

Truncate text with optional expand/collapse functionality.

Props:
- maxChar?: number — max characters (character-based truncation)
- maxLines?: number — max lines (CSS -webkit-line-clamp truncation)
- truncateEnd?: string — appended to truncated text (default: '...')
- expandable?: boolean — show expand/collapse button (default: false)
- expandText?: string — button text when collapsed (default: 'Show more')
- collapseText?: string — button text when expanded (default: 'Show less')
- onToggle?: (isExpanded: boolean) => void — callback on toggle
- children: ReactNode

If content is shorter than the limit, no truncation or button is shown. Character-based mode slices text and appends truncateEnd. Line-based mode uses CSS `-webkit-line-clamp` with `overflow: hidden`.

```tsx
import { Clamp } from 'meemaw';

<Clamp maxChar={100}>
  {longText}
</Clamp>

<Clamp maxLines={3}>
  <p>{article}</p>
</Clamp>

<Clamp
  maxChar={200}
  expandable
  expandText="Read more"
  collapseText="Show less"
  onToggle={(expanded) => console.log(expanded)}
>
  {biography}
</Clamp>
```

## Real-World Examples

### Loading state with data fetching

```tsx
function UserDashboard() {
  const { data, loading, error } = useQuery('/api/dashboard');
  return (
    <Loadable loading={loading} error={error} loadingComponent={<Skeleton />}>
      <Switch>
        <Case when={!data.posts.length}><EmptyState /></Case>
        <Case when={data.posts.length > 0}>
          <Repeat each={data.posts}>
            {post => <PostCard key={post.id} post={post} />}
          </Repeat>
        </Case>
      </Switch>
    </Loadable>
  );
}
```

### Responsive navigation

```tsx
function Navigation() {
  return (
    <>
      <Hidden on={['mobile', 'tablet']}><DesktopNav /></Hidden>
      <Hidden on="desktop"><MobileNav /></Hidden>
    </>
  );
}
```

### First-time user experience

```tsx
function App() {
  return (
    <div>
      <ShowOnce persist persistKey="welcome-v2" persistType="local">
        <WelcomeModal />
      </ShowOnce>
      <Delayed until={userDataLoaded}>
        <MainContent />
      </Delayed>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Role-based content

```tsx
function Dashboard({ user }) {
  return (
    <Switch>
      <Case when={user.role === 'admin'}><AdminDashboard /></Case>
      <Case when={user.role === 'moderator'}><ModeratorDashboard /></Case>
      <Case when={user.role === 'user'}><UserDashboard /></Case>
      <Default><GuestView /></Default>
    </Switch>
  );
}
```

### Code block with copy

```tsx
function CodeBlock({ code, language }) {
  return (
    <div className="code-block">
      <CopyToClipboard text={code}>
        {(copy, copied) => (
          <button onClick={copy}>{copied ? '✓ Copied' : 'Copy'}</button>
        )}
      </CopyToClipboard>
      <pre><code className={language}>{code}</code></pre>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Article preview with clamp

```tsx
function ArticleCard({ article }) {
  return (
    <article>
      <h2>{article.title}</h2>
      <Clamp maxLines={3} expandable expandText="Read more" collapseText="Show less">
        <p>{article.content}</p>
      </Clamp>
    </article>
  );
}
```

## TypeScript

All components ship with full type declarations. Generic support is available for `Repeat<T>`.

```tsx
import { Repeat, ShowOnce, PersistenceType } from 'meemaw';

interface User { id: number; name: string; }
const users: User[] = [/* ... */];

<Repeat<User> each={users}>
  {(user) => <div key={user.id}>{user.name}</div>}
</Repeat>

const persistType: PersistenceType = 'local';
<ShowOnce persist persistType={persistType}>
  <Notification />
</ShowOnce>
```

## Compatibility

- React >= 16.8.0
- SSR frameworks: Next.js, Remix, etc.
- Browsers: Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge (last 2 versions)
- Module formats: CommonJS (.js) and ES Modules (.mjs)
- Tree-shakeable (sideEffects: false)
